extracted.intended_audience: partners implementing EU external actions; recipients of EU funding; implementing partners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recipients and implementing partners on how to acknowledge EU funding and design communication/visibility activities for EU external actions, including branding, budgeting, strategic communication planning, monitoring and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: General obligation to acknowledge origin and ensure visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of EU funding have a general obligation to acknowledge the origin and ensure the visibility of any EU funding received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This obligation applies to all recipients and must be respected when communicating about the funded action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility obligations apply regardless of implementation modality
rubrics_metrics.description: The visibility obligations apply equally, regardless of whether the actions concerned are implemented by the European Commission, through grants and procurement contracts, or partners through indirect management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partners must comply with visibility rules no matter the contractual or management arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: EU emblem is the primary visual brand to acknowledge EU funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The EU emblem is the single most important visual brand used to acknowledge the origin and ensure the visibility of EU funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apart from the emblem, no other visual identity or logo may be created or used to highlight EU support, unless previously agreed with the European Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Gateway logo requirement for Global Gateway projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Partners implementing Global Gateway projects/programmes should also include the Global Gateway logo in addition to the EU emblem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, both the EU emblem and Global Gateway logo must be used together to acknowledge support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on alternative logos without Commission agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Apart from the EU emblem, no other visual identity or logo may be created or used to highlight EU support, unless previously agreed with the European Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek prior agreement from the European Commission before designing or using any additional logos or visual identities to represent EU support.

rubrics_metrics.name: EU emblem must be accompanied by a funding statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The EU emblem should be accompanied by a funding statement (‘Funded by the European Union’ or ‘Co-funded by the European Union’) mentioning the EU’s support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the EU emblem and the funding statement are essential to acknowledge EU support; as a rule, they always go hand in hand and must not be separated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emblem and funding statement must not be separated
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the EU emblem and the funding statement are essential to acknowledge EU support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the visual emblem and the textual funding statement appear together wherever visibility requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility-related expenditure is an eligible cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Visibility counts as an eligible cost. Any expenditure related to visibility is part of the action and can benefit from EU funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because individual projects/programmes will not, in principle, include a dedicated visibility budget, any costs necessary to ensure compliance with contractual visibility requirements should be factored into the budget foreseen for the relevant objectives and activities of the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic communication may be financed for selected political priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain cases, the EU may decide to finance communication actions on selected political priorities as part of a specific programme or project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these cases, communication should help ensure awareness, understanding and perception of the EU and its role in the world, in both the EU and partner countries and regions, is commensurate with the scale, scope and ambition of its sustained engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to produce a Strategic Communication Plan when foreseen
rubrics_metrics.description: When strategic communication activities are foreseen as part of a specific programme or project, the implementing partner should produce a Strategic Communication Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance details the main elements that should be included in this plan (partners should consult the full guidance/PDF for the specified elements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication activities must be data-driven and monitored with KPIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensuring communication activities are data driven is critical to their success. Key performance indicators can be quantitative or qualitative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a good monitoring system, both types of indicators complement each other; use data to shape activities and measure impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve the EU in developing and implementing strategic communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Partners should involve the EU in developing and implementing strategic communication activities, for example press engagement, events or production of audiovisual content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involving the EU helps ensure alignment with the EU’s own strategic communication plans and maximises impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: EU right to use communication material (licence) while ownership remains with recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Union has the right to use communication material produced and owned by the recipients of EU funding. This right is granted in the form of a royalty-free, non-exclusive and irrevocable licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the EU receives a licence to use materials, ownership of the material remains with the recipients of the EU funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: EU will act appropriately and timely in case of non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The EU will act in an appropriate and timely manner in the event of non-compliance by partners of visibility and/or, if relevant, strategic communication obligations, as is the case with any other breach of contractual obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance with visibility/strategic communication obligations may lead to contractual remedies; partners should ensure they meet requirements.
